TEKKEN 8 is an outstanding fighting game. An extremely strong 3D fighter with lots of offline content, strong core mechanics, and all around a fun and stylish game. TEKKEN continues to show the world why it's the winner of the Iron Fist Tournament.
Game balance is wack. If you like guessing as the primary combat mechanic, then this is the game for you.

Its a very nice community and its a fun game to get into and a hard one to get better, so the replayability is high. Even with specific character archetypes, you still have people playing them different every matchup.

3/5 - A fun but disappointing iteration of tekken

If you're a fan of tekken you know what you're getting into. Simple but overwhelming number of knowledge checks. When you get into that perfect flow state in a match, there's no other fighting game quite like it.
There's also a focus on singleplayer and live service offerings like story modes, arcade career(?)-like mode and online hub/social spaces.

But unfortunately. the heat system I think is a step in the wrong direction for tekken. In every round, it narrows the fun unpredictability of hundreds of unique moves to just a few that interact with the heat system.

Granted this happened organically in tekken 7 also when the top players showed how to optimize each character to a fine sheen, but only the top players could afford to play like that in tekken 7 because they had the game knowledge to properly defend against all other knowledge-check based offense.

But in tekken 8 even pros are susceptible to the same pre-canned heat related mix-ups that intermediate players must endure through.

A lose-lose for both pros and intermediate players.

There's still a lot of legacy knowledge carrying over from previous tekkens though. I suspect tekken 8 will remain a top fighting game in terms of players in-spite of the heat system, not because of it.
